prose: The `fetchWithRetry` function attempts to retrieve data from a specified URL by calling the `doFetch` function up to a given number of times (`attempts`). If `doFetch` throws a `std::runtime_error`, indicating a failure, `fetchWithRetry` catches the exception and retries the fetch operation. After exhausting all retry attempts, if no successful fetch occurs, `fetchWithRetry` returns an empty `std::optional<std::string>`. The caller expects either a valid fetched string wrapped in `std::optional` or an empty `std::optional` if all attempts fail. If `fetchWithRetry` were to behave differently—such as not retrying on certain exceptions or returning a default value instead of an empty optional—the observably different outcomes would be fewer retries, potentially unhandled exceptions, or unexpected return values in the calling code.
